summary: Golestan Province is one of Iran's 31 provinces, located in the north-east of the country south of the Caspian Sea, with Gorgan as its capital. It was split from Mazandaran in 1997 and has about 1.7 million people across twelve counties. The note also covers its regional assignment in 2014 and the former name of Gorgan.
one_line: Golestan Province is a north-eastern Iranian province south of the Caspian Sea, capital Gorgan, split from Mazandaran in 1997, with twelve counties.
key_facts: Golestan Province (Persian: استان گلستان, Ostan-e Golestan) is one of the 31 provinces of Iran.
Golestan Province is located in the north-east of Iran, south of the Caspian Sea.
The capital of Golestan Province is Gorgan.
On June 22, 2014, Golestan Province was placed in Region 1 when Iran's provinces were divided into 5 regions solely for coordination and development purposes.
The majority of Golestan Province's population are Sunni Muslims.
Golestan was split off from the province of Mazandaran in 1997.
Golestan Province has a population of 1.7 million (2011).
Golestan Province has an area of 20,380 km².
The province is divided into twelve counties (shahrestans): Aliabad, Aqqala, Azadshahr, Bandar-e Gaz, Gonbad-e Qabus, Gorgan, Kalaleh, Kordkuy, Maraveh Tappeh, Minudasht, Ramian, and Torkaman.
Present-day Gorgan was called Esterabad until 1937.
